subject: Private deployment: operational access & long-retention request — approval needed
messages:
From: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@primerahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@primerahealth.com
Date: 2028-02-15T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Private deployment - operational access & retention asks

Marcus — thanks for the demo last week. Primera is keen to move forward with a Dedicated/Private deployment for our EU tenants, but a couple of non-standard asks came up in procurement and InfoSec that I want to put on the table before we go too far down the contract route:

1) Retention: we need 7 years of encrypted customer data snapshots (timeboxed, quarterly) for regulatory reporting in two member states.
2) Audit access: our auditor (PrimeSec) will request a 10-day forensic access window per year and the ability to export specific log sets.
3) Debug access: because this will be on customer-controlled infra, we need a short-lived (1–2 hour) remote debugging session for Redwood engineers via a customer-managed bastion.
4) KMS/HSM: keys must be customer-managed (BYOK) with support for an HSM provider.

We also have a commercial ask: a 20% discount on list for a 3-year committed contract and a PoC waiver for the first 30 days.

Attached is our security questionnaire (redacted) and a short PoC spec. Can you confirm feasibility and route for approvals?

—Sam
Procurement, Primera Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@primerahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-15T11:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment - operational access & retention asks

Sam — appreciate the clear asks and the attachments. Short answers up front: all are feasible but there are contract and operational tradeoffs we need to lock down. Looping in Legal (Kimberly) and Deal Desk (Jordan) to surface what requires executive signoff.

High-level notes:
- BYOK/HSM: supported in Private deployments; we'll need the KMS integration runbook and an HSM SLA to confirm latency implications.
- Forensic 10-day window: OK as a timeboxed exception, but we'll require a mutual NDA + scoped access checklist and logging of Redwoods engineers' actions.
- Remote debugging: acceptable if routed through the customer's bastion and timeboxed with just-in-time credentials; we will not accept persistent SSH from Redwood.
- 7-year snapshot retention: this is longer than our standard retention for ephemeral PoC artifacts — operational cost and storage pricing will need to be reflected in the quote.

Jordan/Kim: can you advise on discount runway and standard guardrails for the access windows (e.g., audit window notice periods, evidence collection format)? Sam — I'll get a proposed contract carveout summary once Legal confirms the language.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@primerahealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-16T09:47:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment - operational access & retention asks

Hi all — quick clarifying questions from Legal / Compliance before we draft carveouts:

1) Retention scope: Confirm which data classes must be retained for 7 years (customer PII, telemetry, KV cache snapshots?). We prefer to narrow to minimal audit artifacts to reduce exposure.
2) Auditor access: Will PrimeSec access production systems or a forensic copy? Our standard is access to a sanitized, timeboxed forensic copy unless there is lawful process requiring live access.
3) Debugging sessions: Redwood engineers must authenticate with customer-managed MFA and we require an access justification form per session.

Mitigations we recommend to accept these asks without broad risk: timebound clauses (max 10 days/yr for forensic copies), mandatory session recording + immutable audit trail, signed SOC 2 attestation for any third-party auditor access, and storage encryption with customer-controlled keys and documented key-rotation plan.

I will prepare proposed contract language for: (A) limited forensic copy access, (B) just-in-time bastion access with customer session logs, (C) retention scope limited to "audit artifacts" (format definitions), and (D) commercial uplift to cover 7-year storage + HSM support.

-Kim
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-18T14:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment - operational access & retention asks

Marcus / Kim — Deal Desk stance: we can approve a customer-specific carveout for audit access and BYOK, but the commercial uplift needs executive approval if discount request >15% or if we absorb >$120k incremental storage/HSM cost in year 1.

Pricing options to offer Primera (select one to propose to customer):
A) Standard private deployment + HSM add-on: no discount, pass-through HSM + storage costs (baseline).
B) 15% discount with a 2-year commit, customer pays HSM and 7-year storage surcharge (recommended).
C) 25% discount for 3-year commit but Redwood absorbs up to $80k of storage/HSM first-year cost — requires VP-level approval.

Also recommend: DocuSign SOW with a one-sentence executive escalation clause that says any on-prem remote access beyond 2 hours/session requires pre-authorized executive signoff.

If Marcus/Sam want the 20% target, we need Laura's signoff (VP commercial exceptions) and a short rationale (strategic account + expected expansion).

-Jordan
Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-20T10:31:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment - operational access & retention asks

Thanks for the thread. Reviewed commercial and legal tradeoffs. Approve the following exception with conditions:

- Commercial: approve a 20% discount on list for a 3-year committed deal (RDW-2028-0913) contingent on a $1.2M ARR minimum in the first 12 months and an explicit expansion target in year 2.
- Retention: allow 7-year retention limited strictly to "audit artifacts" (schema to be defined by Legal). Redwood to charge a storage surcharge: $0.015 / GB / month for the retained snapshot tier.
- HSM / BYOK: supported — customer must provide HSM SLA and runbook; keys remain under customer control.
- Forensic access: limited to sanitized forensic copies by default; live access only if court order or explicit exec approval. Auditor (PrimeSec) must sign Redwood's auditor addendum and be approved by our Compliance team.
- Remote debugging: allowed only through customer-managed bastion with just-in-time credentials, session recording, and documented sign-off per session (max 3 hours/session).

Kim: please translate the above into contract language and the SOW line items. Jordan: reflect the surcharge and ARR commitment in the quote and include a DocuSign path with a pre-signed executive exceptions form. Marcus: send this package to Sam and close the loop.

-Laura
VP, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@primerahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@primerahealth.com, Aisha Rao <aisha@primesec-audit.com>
Date: 2028-02-22T16:04:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment - operational access & retention asks

Marcus — this is great, thanks to you and the team. Primera accepts the 20% with the ARR/expansion guardrails; PrimeSec will sign the auditor addendum and share the runbook for the bastion. We attached a redline of the PoC scoping doc (see attachment).

Next steps: Marcus to share the finalized SOW + DocuSign link and we'll target signature within 10 business days.

—Sam
